page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a-nps1.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. The configuration supplies 64 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 256 GB of system memory, establishing a standard balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server type does not feature integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs. All persistent file systems and operating system disks must be provisioned through network-attached block storage. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth capacity of 16 Gbps, handling inter-node traffic across cloud infrastructure. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance by default.

From an infrastructure perspective, the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators eliminates secondary hardware cost overhead for workloads that do not require local ephemeral scratch space. The high core count and proportional memory footprint make ecs.g7a-nps1.16xlarge appropriate for enterprise application hosting, container orchestration clusters, distributed continuous integration jobs, and microservices backends relying on external persistent databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a-nps1.16xlarge is a general-purpose KVM-based virtual server designed for multi-threaded workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM. This provides a balanced 1:4 resource allocation of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and contains no local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for operating system and data retention requirements. Network throughput is provisioned with a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Because hardware resources focus strictly on compute cores and standard memory density without specialized accelerator overhead, it serves as a cost-efficient configuration for core-dense enterprise tasks. Typical workloads include large-scale web serving, application tiers, containerized build platforms, and distributed microservices.
